clue.text: Lose ambition and yet score thus

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read literally, to let go of an aim or target
second meaning: a rugby kick through the posts from a ball bounced off the ground

explanation.surface: A paradox: someone gives up all aspiration and still manages to score.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a DROP GOAL is three points kicked from a half-volley in open play; split into two words it means to abandon one's goal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works as a verb phrase for abandoning an aim and as a noun for a rugby scoring kick.

clue.text: Toper endlessly sinks

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a dipso is a heavy drinker, short for dipsomaniac

explanation.surface: A drunkard keeps sinking lower and lower.
explanation.walkthrough: A toper is a drunkard, and DIPSO is the slang shortening; lose its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To dip is to go down or drop, so dips works as a verb meaning goes down or descends.

clue.text: It's an honour to possess old instrument

indicators.note: possessing something means holding it, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: the Order of the British Empire, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone is proud to own an antique musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is an honour awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument in the orchestra.

clue.text: Girl about to chuck in Comprehensive

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to lob is to throw or toss

explanation.surface: A girl is about to give up on her comprehensive school.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British state secondary school, which is the picture; here it is just the adjective meaning all-embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means covering everything, all-inclusive, just as a comprehensive survey does.

clue.text: Certificate of distinction given to one in operation

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these joined pieces sit within another word

parts.note: action, as in a military operation
a credit is a grade of distinction in an exam

explanation.surface: Someone receives a certificate of distinction for their part in an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: A credit is a pass with distinction in British exams; 'given to' simply joins the two pieces before they go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Accreditation is official certification that something meets a standard, much as a certificate attests.

clue.text: A fair old game

parts.note: surface reading: a reasonably good contest, as in 'a fair old game of football'
setter's reading: a fairground, with its traditional ring-tossing stall

explanation.walkthrough: 'A fair old' is a British idiom meaning quite a considerable; the clue really wants an old game played at a funfair, where you throw rings over prizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoop-la is a traditional fairground sideshow where players throw rings to land over prizes.

clue.text: Peculiar traits of one in non-matching neckwear

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first piece sits within the phrase that follows

parts.note: ties that do not match each other are odd

explanation.surface: Someone shows their peculiar habits by wearing mismatched ties.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddities are strange characteristics or quirks, the peculiar traits of an eccentric.

clue.text: Incline? Correct prop round south-east side

indicators.note: to correct is to put right, so these letters are rearranged into proper order

explanation.surface: Instructions for fixing a leaning structure: put a prop round the south-east side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Round' just places the compass letters among the fodder; all of the prop, the south-east and side are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: To predispose is to make someone inclined or liable towards something in advance.

clue.text: Sitting-room with a view?

parts.note: surface reading: a lounge in a house with a pleasant outlook
setter's reading: a room where many people sit in order to watch and hear a performance

explanation.walkthrough: A sitting-room is normally a lounge; here it is literally a room for sitting, with a view of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditorium is the part of a theatre or hall where the audience is seated to watch.

clue.text: Born with Scorpio's wrinkled nose

indicators.note: something wrinkled is creased out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Astrology joke: anyone born under Scorpio gets a wrinkled nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A proboscis is a long nose or snout, used humorously of a large human nose.

clue.text: Magistrates getting gratuity in money on the records

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first piece goes within the word for money

parts.note: a sen is a small Japanese coin

explanation.surface: Magistrates are on record receiving bribes, a corruption scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: The sen is a hundredth of a Japanese yen. Stipendiaries are paid professional magistrates, as opposed to unpaid lay justices.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipendiary is a salaried magistrate, so the plural names a group of paid judicial officers.

clue.text: Fear adder is let loose

indicators.note: something let loose runs wild, so the letters escape their order

explanation.surface: Panic as a venomous snake escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Like ad broadcast at precisely defined tourist area

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: strict, as in a strict definition

explanation.surface: A tourist board airs an advertisement for a carefully delimited holiday region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lake District is a mountainous national park in Cumbria, north-west England, popular with walkers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake District is a famous English holiday region visited by millions of sightseers each year.

clue.text: Sort of manor house in ancient times

definitions.text: Sort of manor house in ancient times

indicators.note: to sort is to rearrange, so the letters of the next word are put in another order

parts.note: a villa is a country house

explanation.surface: A description of a stately home as it was in the classical world.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is 'Sort of manor house'; 'in ancient times' completes the whole clue as a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman villa was the country estate house of a wealthy Roman, a manor of classical antiquity.

clue.text: Money Lianne used for special anniversary

indicators.note: used here means worked over or knocked about, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Lianne spends cash on a celebration for a big anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: A centennial is a hundredth anniversary, certainly a special one worth celebrating.

clue.text: River direction not right

indicators.note: not right says the letter standing for right is removed

parts.note: an order is a direction or instruction

explanation.surface: Someone on a river is told which way to go and it is the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a major central European river forming part of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Man with English bodyguard at the ringside?

definitions.note: elliptical for 'one at the ringside', a noun

explanation.surface: A boxer's minder accompanies him ringside with his English bodyguard.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: in boxing the official who times the rounds sits at the ringside.
explanation.definitionFit: A timekeeper sits beside a boxing ring to time each round and ring the bell.

clue.text: Discontinue meeting in favour of a rascal

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A meeting is called off by people who back a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue is to suspend a parliament's session without dissolving it, so ending a sitting.

clue.text: Drawback in pudding produced later

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the turned word goes within the dessert

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert

indicators.note: back means turned the other way, so that word is read from right to left

parts.note: the single word splits into draw and back; only the first part supplies letters

explanation.surface: There is a snag in the dessert that came later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' looks like one word meaning snag; split it into draw and back. Afters is everyday British for the pudding course.
explanation.definitionFit: Afterwards and later are both adverbs meaning at a subsequent time.

clue.text: Hairy one of the sauropods

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the letters lie inside the next words

explanation.surface: A shaggy dinosaur among the long-necked giants.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, Jacob's twin brother is described as a hairy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Esau in the Bible is famously hairy, the brother Jacob impersonated with goatskins.

clue.text: Demonstrator loses head: he takes a bow!

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is taken away

explanation.surface: A protester is beheaded, and then, like a performer, takes a bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes a bow' suggests acknowledging applause; here it means picking up a longbow.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer is someone who shoots arrows from a bow, so he literally carries one.

clue.text: Could offering this produce a "No" in one driver?

definitions.text: Could offering this produce a "No" in one driver?

indicators.note: to produce is to make something new, so these letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Would a driver refuse if offered a glass of wine?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a motorist offered cheap wine would sensibly say no.
explanation.definitionFit: Vin ordinaire is cheap everyday French table wine, the kind one might offer a guest.

clue.text: He's top man; it stands out

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the person in charge
second meaning: a raised knob or stud, as on a shield

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the round projecting stud in the middle of a shield or a carved ornament on a ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a manager or chief and a protruding ornamental knob.

clue.text: Section of choirboys uplifted the spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
a section is a part, so the letters are cut from inside the next word

parts.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.surface: Part of the choir raised everyone's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour or liveliness, the spirit and dash of a performance.

clue.text: Fellow leaving operation of aircraft and remaining on the ground

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the word

explanation.surface: A pilot quits flying and stays grounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying describes something resting flat, stretched out rather than standing or airborne.

clue.text: Close acquaintance staying after gangster leaves the area

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so that word departs from the larger one

explanation.surface: A friend remains in the district once the local mobster has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is what is left staying behind after the hood departs.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is a person living close by, often known but not intimate.

clue.text: Having dropped off, like covering to be put back

indicators.note: put back means turned round, so that word runs the other way

parts.note: peel is the skin covering fruit

explanation.surface: Something has fallen off, like a cover that needs replacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping off is an idiom for falling into sleep, so someone who has done so is sleeping.

clue.text: Esso reps produce the drink

indicators.note: to produce is to make something new, so these letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Sales representatives from the oil company make the coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: Esso is a petrol brand, used here only for its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.
